topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, outlining course themes, student backgrounds, and specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Differentiation and Genetic Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the nature of cancer as an accumulation of genetic alterations leading to a failure of normal developmental differentiation and tissue architecture, along with the laboratory approaches used to study tumor cells.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Benign versus Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between benign and malignant tumors, detailing how cellular invasion and metastasis progress histologically from precursor lesions.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the rules and conventions of tumor nomenclature used to classify neoplasms according to their tissue origin and malignant potential.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Disease and Mortality in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the mechanical, physiological, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Comparative Incidence of Cancer in Humans and Animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distribution and frequency of cancer types across human populations and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Principles and Applications of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale, histological basis, and relative effectiveness of population screening and early detection across different cancer types.

topics.label: Closing and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing remarks, summarizing the lecture's learning objectives and previewing upcoming practicals and sessions.
